PullRequest.Title: Support Copilot policy helper timeout and failure mode
PullRequest.Body:
### Agent assessment Self-reported assessment, not an independent review. Assessed revision: `dff4369a15ba60aab5033edc05150848a26d8b6c` | Dimension | Assessment | Rationale | |---|---|---| | Change confidence | 8/10 | ↑ Incremental client build and changed-file lint passed.
↑ Affected suites reported 249 passes and one pending test.
↑ Signed-in chats and delayed-helper checks passed on the earlier implementation.
↓ Electron did not exit after the test summary.
↓ The bundled runtime ignores the failure-mode override.
↓ A combined argument/mode refresh remains unisolated. | | Diagnosis confidence | 9.5/10 | ↑ Registration normalization discarded `timeoutMs` before runtime startup.
↑ Real-runtime probes demonstrated timeout preservation.
↑ All four deadline regression cases failed before the fix and passed afterward. | | Evidence fit | 8.5/10 | ↑ The delayed helper failed with the default timeout and completed with `timeoutMs: 30000`.
↑ Runtime source confirms that directory-specific resolution awaits helper execution.
↓ A complete third-party helper, plugin, and skill workflow was not exercised. | ## Changes - Preserve optional integer `timeoutMs` values from 1 through 30000 in the local Copilot policy-helper registration. Omission retains the runtime's 5000 ms default. - Add `chat.agentHost.copilot.policyHelperFailureMode` with `null`, `ignore`, and `failClosed`. Null removes the local environment override. Device and server policy precedence remains runtime-owned. - Include the failure mode in startup comparison and child environment construction. Changes use the existing restart boundary after active turns and subagents finish. - Use one 45000 ms host deadline for both managed-settings resolution paths. The runtime helper limit remains 30000 ms. Both settings remain local to the application and excluded from Settings Sync. ## Runtime compatibility The bundled runtime 1.0.114 does not read `COPILOT_CLI_POLICY_HELPER_FAILURE_MODE`. The setting description states this limitation. This expected no-op behavior is accepted for this change. Enforcement requires runtime support and a VS Code dependency update that includes it. This PR does not change dependency versions or implement enforcement in VS Code. ## Validation On base `2219f59cf7c96358f40dac5a4aeda3fa7af85c6d`, `pnpm run build-fast --client-only` passed. The focused test command below passed all 27 tests before the deadline follow-up. ```powershell pnpm run build-fast --client-only .\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\common\copilotCliConfig.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\copilotAgentStartupConfig.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\copilotAgent.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\chatConfiguration.test.ts --grep "copilotCliConfig|CopilotAgentStartupConfig|CopilotAgent .*policy helper|Chat configuration .*policy helper" --reporter dot ``` For the final deadline follow-up, these exact commands ran: ```powershell node build\oxlint.ts src\vs\platform\agentHost\node\copilot\copilotManagedSettings.ts src\vs\platform\agentHost\node\copilot\copilotSessionLauncher.ts src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\copilotManagedSettings.test.ts src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\copilotSessionLauncher.test.ts node build\next\build-fast.ts --client-only .\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\copilotManagedSettings.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\copilotSessionLauncher.test.ts --grep "Copilot managed settings resolution|CopilotSessionLauncher" --reporter dot ``` Lint and the incremental client build passed. The affected test suites reported 249 passes and one pending test. The Electron harness did not exit after the summary. Its owned process tree was stopped. A clean harness exit remains unverified. The four upper-bound regression cases failed against the original deadline and passed with the shared 45000 ms deadline. The earlier `pnpm run build-fast` product build passed on base `066b95e79643685c1bbbadec58f86b0d212bb1b6`. The signed-in UI checks also ran on that base. - Two minimal chat requests completed with `OK.`. - A synthetic helper with a 6500 ms delay never completed under the default timeout. With `timeoutMs: 30000`, it completed in 6510 ms. - Timeout changes and removal restarted the SDK. Changes through `failClosed`, `ignore`, and `null` also restarted the SDK. The isolated app and profile were removed after these checks. The normal editor profile was unchanged. ## Limits The full type check did not complete during prerequisite setup and was not rerun. Live busy-turn and subagent restart deferral was not exercised. During one combined argument/failure-mode edit, the helper's argument marker remained unchanged until a later timeout edit. The cause remains unisolated. The existing argument transport and comparison code is unchanged. No linked issue.

Scenarios.Scenario: Mirror local policy-helper settings from the workbench to the agent host
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On connection or a relevant application/user configuration event, normalize values, construct a root-config patch and dispatch it to the connected host. No helper execution is added to workbench configuration processing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch one combined root-configuration patch containing applicable changed settings.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One dispatch per applicable configuration event per connected local-host client; changing helper registration and failure mode together puts both keys in the same patch. Remote targets exclude both settings.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same configuration listener already grouped changed settings into a single patch. The diff adds a bounded enum value and optional numeric registration field, not a dispatch per field.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Configuration must reach the host before startup comparison can apply it; patch dispatch does not await policy-helper execution.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Normalize and transport helper registration and the failure-mode reset value.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bounded scalar addition to an existing helper object, plus one enum/reset string; existing path/argument traversal is unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Registration already underwent schema validation and transport. Path and arguments were already serialized; timeoutMs was discarded.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Small synchronous transformation before existing protocol transport.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of connected local-host clients and relevant configuration events; no per-workspace-file or per-chat iteration is added.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Settings affected by one event are grouped in one patch. Existing transport scheduling is unchanged.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache. Local-only scope prevents propagation to remote hosts. Normalization produces stable helper property ordering and stable empty/reset representations.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected transforms, target filtering, root-patch construction and the protocol client's grouping loop.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual configuration-event frequency varies, but the added payload and normalization work are bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: no added boundary fan-out, unbounded payload or synchronous expensive operation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start or restart the Copilot runtime after helper timeout or failure-mode changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Capture startup config, load certificates and runtime assets, build the child environment, then await client.start(). Changed effective settings request a restart only after active turns, subagents and credential updates finish.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stop an existing SDK runtime and start its replacement using RuntimeConnection.forSpawnedStdio.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Effective timeout/failure-mode changes can cause a restart; equivalent normalized settings do not. Busy-period requests are parked until idle. Concurrent legacy acquisitions share one start/healing sequence; stale-start recovery permits one retry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Helper path/argument edits already used this restart mechanism. The diff deliberately adds timeout and failure-mode changes as startup-affecting inputs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A replacement must start before dependent SDK operations proceed; ongoing turns and subagents are not interrupted to apply these settings.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve SDK platform assets with realpath/access checks and load or materialize configured certificates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing per-start asset lookup: one SDK realpath plus five parallel existence checks per candidate platform package, stopping at a successful package; certificate work remains conditional.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical prerequisites occurred on every runtime start. New explicit setting changes can invoke the existing restart path, but unrelated and equivalent configuration values do not.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required startup prerequisites; independent asset operations remain concurrent.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Actual effective setting changes and existing client scopes, not ordinary configuration notifications or message count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Legacy starts and their bounded retry sequence are coalesced. Restarts wait for existing stop operations and defer past in-flight work. Scoped clients retain their existing independent ownership.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm legacy clients are returned without restarting. Startup equality includes a primitive failure mode and deterministic helper JSON; scoped-client startup snapshots also compare the new field. Runtime asset lookup is existing per-start work.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for restart triggers, coalescing, busy-work deferral and retry bounds; runtime-internal initialization is outside the visible source.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Runtime spawn duration and the number of credential-scoped clients vary. Failure-mode support in a selected external runtime cannot be verified from these repository files.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the added restart triggers are explicit startup-setting semantics, with existing equality, deferral and bounded retry safeguards preserved.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create or resume a chat with managed policy, including a slow configured helper
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing plugin/tool preparation completes, managedSettings.resolve is awaited before approval policy and session creation/resumption, and the normal SDK launch then proceeds. Both shared and direct policy paths now allow 45 seconds rather than 30; the runtime helper registration accepts an explicit limit of at most 30 seconds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Ask the spawned runtime to resolve managed settings for the account and optional working directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Shared resolver issues one request per simultaneously pending (RPC object, account token, working directory) tuple. Direct fallback issues one request per invocation. Both counts are unchanged by this PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same policy request and ordering already existed with a 30-second host deadline. Helper registration omitted timeoutMs, leaving the runtime default.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Policy remains a prerequisite for SDK session creation/resumption. Successful responses complete immediately; only the outer maximum wait changes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Existing runtime-owned policy resolution can execute the registered policy helper.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The host's policy-request cardinality is unchanged. Exact helper execution/cache-hit counts are runtime-owned and not visible in repository source; preserving timeoutMs changes an individual run's allowed duration, not a host-side loop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Helper execution was already enabled by the same registration/environment path; explicit timeout values were previously dropped.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Helper-dependent policy resolution can delay launch; the 45-second host cap leaves headroom for the explicitly permitted 30-second helper limit.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read custom-agent content, check plugin directories, optionally read prompt overrides, and resolve the runtime working directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing work scales with configured agents/plugins; plugin directory checks are launched together with other independent session prerequisites. No additional read or changed placement is introduced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same filesystem operations and parallel preparation existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing launch prerequisites retain their ordering, including prompt override reads after policy.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct concurrent client/account/working-directory tuples after in-flight grouping, plus pre-existing configured plugin/agent counts.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Concurrent identical shared requests join one promise; distinct tuples can run concurrently without a new global limiter. Direct fallback remains uncoalesced as before. Independent plugin/tool preparation remains Promise.all-based.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Shared resolver caches only in-flight work and removes entries on success, error or timeout. Completed policy freshness and server/helper cache fallback remain runtime-owned. Cancellation detaches a caller without cancelling other waiters; invalidation/disposal cancels the generation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the existing critical-path RPC, effective grouping and the exact 30-to-45-second deadline change; runtime-internal boundary multiplicity is not established.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Helper duration, runtime cache behavior and server-policy network work depend on the external runtime and deployment. No measured latency is inferred.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the larger bounded deadline intentionally accommodates newly preserved helper timeouts. It adds no requests or unconditional delay to successful resolutions; independently unintended performance harm is not established.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resolve chat configuration and refresh disconnected chats' approval modes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: resolveChatConfig acquires the SDK client and awaits managed policy before returning approval configuration. After runtime startup, disconnected-chat approval reconciliation runs in the background rather than being awaited by startup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve policy for a requested chat configuration or for disconnected chat owners after startup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Background reconciliation first deduplicates owner resources, then the shared resolver groups overlapping requests by runtime RPC object, token and working directory. Many owners sharing one directory can therefore share one pending RPC; separate directories remain separate requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same deduplication, Promise.all reconciliation, in-flight grouping and bounded retry on client replacement existed. Only the shared host deadline and explicitly supplied helper timeout change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Direct configuration resolution waits for policy. Startup invokes disconnected reconciliation with void, keeping that pass off the startup completion path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct eligible disconnected owners, reduced at the RPC boundary to distinct concurrent account/working-directory tuples.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Distinct owner reconciliations use Promise.all, but equal policy keys coalesce. This is unchanged, and the diff introduces no new iteration or concurrent batch.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Only pending policy work is shared; no completed or negative cache is added. Client replacement invalidates pending context. Warm unchanged clients avoid startup acquisition cost.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced the owner ResourceSet, eligibility checks, shared resolver and background invocation at client startup.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Number of distinct directories and external helper/server latency vary; runtime-owned filesystem/network composition cannot be counted from host code.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: existing fan-out is neither introduced nor increased. A longer failure deadline alone, with required helper headroom, does not establish an actionable independent regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Refresh model catalogs, change a model and update per-session model-policy metadata
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Catalog refresh lists models then resolves managed policy before publishing the replacement catalog. An explicit model change awaits policy before setModel. Session model-configuration metadata refresh is fire-and-forget and awaits policy followed by model.list/getCurrent.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List the runtime model catalog, resolve managed policy, and apply a requested model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One catalog-list RPC and one policy request per effective catalog refresh, not per model. Credential-scoped catalog discovery shares its stored promise/results per credential source and startup snapshot. Model changes issue policy requests per operation, subject to existing in-flight policy grouping.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same listing, policy and model-setting calls in the same order. No new per-model request was added.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Catalog publication and explicit model selection remain dependent on policy; periodic refresh preserves the last-known catalog on failure.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh managed policy, then session.model.list and session.model.getCurrent to publish model-configuration metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A pre-existing per-session Throttler bounds the refresh queue; each executed refresh has one policy resolution followed by two model RPCs. The PR does not add refresh triggers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical background refresh work and throttling existed; shared/direct policy deadline changes from 30 to 45 seconds.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background metadata work is not awaited by refreshModelConfiguration callers.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The external runtime retrieves model/service metadata and composes remote managed policy behind existing RPCs, using existing proxy/authentication callbacks as needed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Host-level catalog and policy request counts are unchanged; exact server requests, retries and cache hits are runtime-owned and not visible in the reviewed source.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same external-runtime service operations and network configuration; dependency versions are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing catalog/policy network dependencies remain on refresh paths; the diff does not add a network call or move one earlier.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective catalog refreshes, credential sources and explicit model changes; not the number of models returned. Session metadata refresh bursts are reduced by the existing Throttler.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Legacy model refreshes coalesce, scoped sources remain independent, chat operations use their existing sequencing, and background metadata refreshes use per-session throttling. Distinct policy tuples remain independently concurrent.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Legacy periodic model refresh joins existing scheduled/in-flight work; lifecycle refreshes are scheduled together. Credential catalogs reuse per-source promises until credentials/startup snapshots change and delete failed entries. Policy results themselves are not host-cached after completion.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for critical paths, request cardinality and host-side coalescing; no claim is made about unseen runtime cache internals or measured duration.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Catalog size, scoped-source count and runtime/network latency are deployment-specific. The increased worst-case failure wait is known, but normal successful work is not forced to wait longer.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the diff changes accepted startup metadata and timeout headroom, not refresh frequency, per-model boundary count, queue structure or cache retention.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all 12 changed files and all diff pages against base 2219f59cf7c96358f40dac5a4aeda3fa7af85c6d. Traced configuration grouping, startup/restart ownership, policy resolution, launch/resume, disconnected-chat reconciliation and model workflows. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance bug or independently proven performance-regression fix qualified. Static source analysis cannot establish external runtime helper/server cache internals or measured timings.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
